analysis: All units are documentation or changelog only: two new changelog.d fragments, a paragraph in docs/developer/build.md (head lines 26-30) and a new section in docs/developer/test.md (head lines 17-28). No executable code changed, and no trust-boundary, key, attestation, routing or authorization code is modified in the supplied evidence. The provider status/doctor Swift changes and ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests that the docs describe are not in this batch, so I could not check them. The docs are consistent with TB-011 and T-057. Status and doctor now show an unexpired App Attest lease, which is a display-only change that grants no serving permission (T-052, T-058). MDM removal advice requires a fresh decision, and the 30-second ReceiptDecisionFreshness and 24-hour receipt renewal bounds are described unchanged. The changelog says `darkbloom unenroll` is unchanged and still requires a renewal within 10 seconds. That agrees with TB-011's rule that removal guidance needs a fresh coordinator decision. Remaining questions for integration: the actual freshness logic in status, doctor and unenroll lives in other batches. A reviewer there should confirm that showing App Attest authorization for a late-but-unexpired lease cannot be mistaken for removal readiness. They should also confirm that the removal advice path still gates on the fresh receipt decision, so MDM removal is not offered with stale evidence (T-057, T-053). No threat-model update appears needed from the docs alone.
